title: Fix GatedDeltaNet A_log dtype to prevent -inf under bfloat16 init
body:
# What does this PR do?

`Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet`, `Qwen3_5MoeGatedDeltaNet`, and `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` sample `A_log` via:

```python
A = torch.empty(self.num_v_heads).uniform_(0, 16)
self.A_log = nn.Parameter(torch.log(A))
```

and re-sample it the same way in each model's `_init_weights`. When the model is initialized under a `bfloat16` default dtype (e.g., `.from_config(config, dtype=torch.bfloat16)`), `uniform_(0, 16)` can round a sampled value down to `0`, and `log(0) == -inf`. That `-inf` gets baked into `A_log`, permanently zeroing that head's decay term and freezing its gradient for the rest of training.

This PR samples `A` in `float32` explicitly (independent of the ambient default dtype) before taking the log, in both the module constructor and `_init_weights`, for all three affected models mentioned above.

It also adds a regression test (`test_gated_delta_net_a_log_finite_under_bfloat16_init`) for each of the three affected models asserting `A_log` stays `float32` and finite when the model is constructed with `dtype=torch.bfloat16`. I ran the full test suite for all three models locally with no regressions:

- `tests/models/qwen3_5/test_modeling_qwen3_5.py`: 292 passed, 232 skipped
- `tests/models/qwen3_5_moe/test_modeling_qwen3_5_moe.py`: 296 passed, 220 skipped
- `tests/models/qwen3_next/test_modeling_qwen3_next.py`: 148 passed, 145 skipped

Fixes #47831

title: nemotron_h (Nemotron 3.5 Lightning): silently wrong outputs under multi-GPU device_map dispatch — cache corruption + split-boundary-dependent garbage; fused kernel path crashes under hooks
body:
## System Info

- `transformers`: 5.15.0 and `main` (5.16.0.dev0) — identical behavior on both
- `torch`: 2.11.0+cu130, `accelerate` (bundled dispatch), Python 3.12
- Hardware: 4× NVIDIA 48GB GPUs (Ampere/Ada mix), 1TB RAM
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16` (hybrid Mamba-2 + latent-MoE, `model_type: nemotron_h`)
- `mamba-ssm`/`causal-conv1d`: absent for the main repro (torch-native path); crash report below is with them installed (2.3.2.post1, built vs CUDA 13.0)

## Summary

The model card's own quickstart (`AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., device_map="auto")`)
produces **near-random outputs with no error or warning** on a multi-GPU box.
The weights are fine (llama.cpp runs the same checkpoint coherently; a CPU
single-device forward through transformers is also correct). Three separable
defects:

### 1. `use_cache=True` (the default, even for loss-only forwards) corrupts the hybrid scan cache across device boundaries

With the model dispatched across 2 GPUs and a plain
`model(input_ids, labels=input_ids)` forward (cache defaults on), loss on
ordinary English text is ~10 (near-random for a 131k vocab) and greedy
generation is token salad. The identical call with `use_cache=False` gives
sane loss (2.6–3.0). No warning is emitted in either case.

### 2. Even with `use_cache=False`, correctness depends on where the auto device-map places split boundaries

Same script, same 512-token English input, only `max_memory` varied:

| placement | forward loss |
|---|---|
| CPU only (single device) | 3.03 ✅ |
| 2 GPUs (`{0:"46GiB",1:"46GiB"}`) | 2.66 ✅ |
| 3 GPUs | 10.23 ❌ |
| 4 GPUs | 9.51 ❌ |

Some boundary placements evidently sever Mamba/latent state that must stay
device-local. Silent in all cases.

### 3. Fused kernel path crashes under dispatch hooks

With `mamba-ssm` + `causal-conv1d` installed, any multi-GPU forward
(cache on or off, 2 or 4 GPUs, weights verified GPU-resident) dies in the
chunk-scan Triton kernel:

```
ValueError: Pointer argument (at 0) cannot be accessed from Triton (cpu tensor?)
```

This looks like a device-context/current-device mismatch when the kernel is
launched from a layer accelerate has hooked, rather than a genuinely-CPU
tensor (a post-dispatch sweep found zero misplaced parameters or buffers).

## Reproduction

```python
import sys
# force the torch-native path for defects 1–2
sys.modules["mamba_ssm"] = None
sys.modules["causal_conv1d"] = None
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

M = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(M)
text = open("any_english_text.txt").read()  # a few paragraphs of prose
ids = tok(text, return_tensors="pt")["input_ids"][:, :512]

for mm in (None,                                   # CPU: device_map="cpu"
           {0: "46GiB", 1: "46GiB"},               # 2 GPUs: sane
           {0: "42GiB", 1: "42GiB", 2: "42GiB"}):  # 3 GPUs: garbage
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        M, dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        device_map="cpu" if mm is None else "auto", max_memory=mm)
    x = ids.to(model.device)
    for cache in (True, False):
        with torch.no_grad():
            loss = model(x, labels=x, use_cache=cache).loss.item()
        print(mm, "cache:", cache, "loss:", round(loss, 3))
    del model; torch.cuda.empty_cache()
```

Expected: ~3.0 everywhere. Observed: ~3.0 only on CPU and (cache-off) 2-GPU;
~9.5–10.6 otherwise.

## Additional observations (same module, possibly separate issues)

- Config round-trip is lossy: `NemotronHConfig.from_pretrained` →
  `save_pretrained` drops `num_hidden_layers` and rewrites
  `layers_block_type` `'mamba'`→`'linear_attention'`; the re-serialized
  config then breaks external consumers (e.g. llama.cpp's converter).
- `save_pretrained` silently discards the checkpoint's 270 `mtp.*` tensors
  (the class doesn't model the MTP block) — a merged/fine-tuned save is
  missing weights relative to the source with no warning.
- Related open issue in the same port: #47246 (incorrect inter-chunk
  recurrence in `NemotronHMamba2Mixer.torch_forward`). Note the repro above
  is a *different* defect: at a fixed sequence length on a single device the
  slow path is self-consistent, while the failures here appear/disappear
  purely with device placement.

Happy to run patches against this setup.

title: Fix Gemma `sliding_window` being halved on every config save/reload
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47940)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47940)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

`Gemma3TextConfig.__post_init__` converts the declared sliding window into the exclusive
half-window the attention kernels use, and writes the result back into the field it read from:

```python
if self.use_bidirectional_attention:
    self.sliding_window = (self.sliding_window // 2) + 1  # due to fa we set exclusive bounds
```

`save_pretrained` then persists the converted value, and the next load converts it again, so the
window halves on every save/load round trip. No model download is needed to reproduce it:

```python
from transformers import Gemma3TextConfig

config = Gemma3TextConfig(sliding_window=512, use_bidirectional_attention=True)
print(config.sliding_window)                                          # 257
config.save_pretrained("/tmp/cfg")                                    # writes "sliding_window": 257
print(Gemma3TextConfig.from_pretrained("/tmp/cfg").sliding_window)    # 129
```

Repeating the cycle gives `512 -> 257 -> 129 -> 65 -> 33 -> 17 -> 9 -> 5 -> 3 -> 2`, and 2 is a
fixed point, so the window keeps shrinking until attention is effectively local to one token.

`google/embeddinggemma-300m` ships `"sliding_window": 512` in its `config.json`, so the value
`save_pretrained` writes back is not the convention the checkpoint itself uses.

## Where it comes from

Introduced in #40700 (`948bc0fa`). Before it, #40694 divided in the mask overlay
(`abs(q_idx - kv_idx) <= sliding_window // 2`) and left the config untouched. #40700 moved the
division to config init so that flash-attention — which reads `config.sliding_window` for its
`window_size` and never builds a mask — agrees with eager/sdpa/flex. That consolidation is
correct and this PR keeps it; the only problem is that the converted value is also the one that
gets serialized.

## Impact

Every `save_pretrained` / `from_pretrained` cycle on a bidirectional Gemma config is affected:
fine-tuning checkpoints, PEFT merges, quantization exports, and re-uploads to the Hub, which then
carry the halved window permanently.

Measured on a `google/embeddinggemma-300m` checkpoint round-tripped through `save_pretrained`,
with its weights verified bit-identical to the source (314/314 tensors), evaluated with
`sentence-transformers` on NanoBEIR:

| | mean nDCG@10 | nfcorpus | scifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| source checkpoint | 0.6271558738396297 | 0.3929820955134049 | 0.8613296521658544 |
| after one round trip | 0.6184786921356261 | — | — |
| round trip, `sliding_window` patched back to 512 | 0.6271558738396297 | 0.3929820955134049 | 0.8613296521658544 |

The weights are identical in all three rows, so the 0.87 pp is the config scalar alone; patching
only that field reproduces the baseline exactly to 16 significant digits on both datasets.

## Fix

`to_dict()` serializes the value `__post_init__` converted *from*, so a saved config reloads to
the in-memory window instead of being halved a second time.

This mirrors `ModernBertConfig`, which keeps the declared window in the serialized field and
exposes the converted one as a
[`sliding_window` property](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/modernbert/modular_modernbert.py#L181-L189).
Gemma cannot use that split because its checkpoints already serialize the key as
`sliding_window`, so the conversion is undone at serialization time instead.

`(sliding_window - 1) * 2` is an exact pre-image of `v // 2 + 1`, since `((2c - 2) // 2) + 1 == c`
for every integer `c`. For an even declared window — every released Gemma checkpoint — it
recovers the original value exactly (`512 -> 257 -> 512`). An odd declared window comes back one
lower, which reloads to the same in-memory value.

In-memory behaviour is unchanged: masking, attention and cache still see the converted window.
Configs that do not convert (`use_bidirectional_attention` false / `None` / `"vision"`) serialize
byte-for-byte as before.

The guard uses `getattr` because `Gemma3nTextConfig`, `T5Gemma2TextConfig` and
`T5Gemma2DecoderConfig` inherit `Gemma3TextConfig` through modular while overriding
`__post_init__` to drop the conversion, and do not define the flag at all — the same reason
`Gemma4TextConfig.__post_init__` already reads `getattr(self, "attention_k_eq_v", True)`. Their
regenerated files carry the method as a no-op.

## Compatibility

- A newly saved config stores the declared window (`512`) where it previously stored the
  converted one (`257`). Loading it through `transformers` yields `257` either way.
- Configs already saved with the converted value cannot be repaired: `257` as a declared window
  and `257` as a converted one are indistinguishable. They still load as `129`, but they no
  longer decay further on subsequent saves.

Happy to add the 🚨 prefix to the title if you consider the changed serialized value breaking.

## Alternatives considered

- Moving the division back to the mask overlay would reintroduce the flash-attention / mask
  divergence that #40700 fixed.
- Making `__post_init__` idempotent needs extra state, and private attributes are serialized too
  (`_sliding_window_pattern` ends up in `config.json`), so it would add a key to every file.

Happy to move this into `PreTrainedConfig` instead if you would prefer a general mechanism for
`__post_init__` normalisations that are not idempotent.

## Tests

`test_bidirectional_sliding_window_survives_save_and_reload` in the Gemma3 and Gemma4 text model
tests, one per hand-written config source. Both fail on `main` with `AssertionError: 129 != 257`.

`Gemma4UnifiedTextConfig` and `DiffusionGemmaTextConfig` carry the same `__post_init__` line
through modular inheritance from `Gemma4TextConfig`; their configuration files were regenerated.
All seven config classes that end up with the new method — the four that convert and the three
that inherit it inert — were checked for save/reload stability over three consecutive round trips.

## Before submitting

- [x] This PR fixes a bug.
- [x] Did you read the [contributor guideline](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/contributing)?
- [x] Did you write any new necessary tests? Yes, one per affected config source.
- [x] The generated configuration files were regenerated from their modular files.

## Who can review?

@vasqu (author of #40700) and @Cyrilvallez.

title: Support sdpa/eager attention dispatch in TimmWrapper
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47939)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47939)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #47917

## What's the problem

`TimmWrapperPreTrainedModel` inherits `_supports_sdpa = False`, so loading any model with a timm
backbone and `attn_implementation="sdpa"` raises:

```
ValueError: TimmWrapperModel does not support an attention implementation through
torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention yet.
```

The flag is also inaccurate: timm attention layers already dispatch to
`F.scaled_dot_product_attention` by default. So on `main` the wrapper reports `eager` while it is
actually running fused attention — `attn_implementation` is silently ignored either way.

Passing a dict (`attn_implementation={"vision_config": "eager", ...}`) works around the crash, but
it does not fix the mismatch: the timm backbone still runs SDPA regardless of what the config says.

## Approach

timm resolves the fused-attention decision once at module creation time and caches it per attention
module as `module.fused_attn`. Toggling that attribute therefore only affects the model instance at
hand — unlike `timm.layers.set_fused_attn` / `TIMM_FUSED_ATTN`, which are process-global and would
leak into unrelated timm models.

So the wrapper now declares SDPA support and propagates the resolved `attn_implementation` down to
the wrapped timm model's attention modules, both at init and when it is changed later (including
when a parent multimodal model dispatches implementations to its sub-models). Architectures without
attention layers (convnets) are left untouched, and unsupported backends such as
`flash_attention_2` keep raising as before.

## Before / after

```python
import torch
from transformers import TimmWrapperConfig, TimmWrapperModel


def fused_attn_flags(model):
    return {m.fused_attn for m in model.timm_model.modules() if hasattr(m, "fused_attn")}


for requested in (None, "sdpa", "eager"):
    config = TimmWrapperConfig(architecture="vit_tiny_patch16_224")
    model = TimmWrapperModel._from_config(config, attn_implementation=requested)
    print(f"requested={requested!r:8} -> config={model.config._attn_implementation:5} timm fused_attn={fused_attn_flags(model)}")

pixel_values = torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)
model.set_attn_implementation("sdpa")
sdpa_out = model(pixel_values).last_hidden_state
model.set_attn_implementation("eager")
eager_out = model(pixel_values).last_hidden_state
print("max abs diff (sdpa vs eager):", (sdpa_out - eager_out).abs().max().item())
```

Before — the default silently falls back to `eager` while timm still runs fused attention, and an
explicit request crashes:

```
requested=None     -> config=eager timm fused_attn={True}
ValueError: TimmWrapperModel does not support an attention implementation through
torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention yet.
```

After — the config matches what timm actually runs, and `eager` is now a real fallback:

```
requested=None     -> config=sdpa  timm fused_attn={True}
requested='sdpa'   -> config=sdpa  timm fused_attn={True}
requested='eager'  -> config=eager timm fused_attn={False}
max abs diff (sdpa vs eager): 2.384185791015625e-06
```

The MRE from the issue also loads fine now:

```bash
python -c "from transformers import AutoModel; AutoModel.from_pretrained('facebook/Perception-LM-1B', attn_implementation='sdpa')"
```

## Tests

`tests/models/timm_wrapper/` — 82 passed, 3 failed. The 3 failures (`test_cpu_offload`,
`test_disk_offload_bin`, `test_disk_offload_safetensors`) reproduce identically on the base commit
and are unrelated to this change.

Restructures the vLLM CI workflow to fix persistent OOM failures and adds dedicated matrix jobs for better isolation and parallelism.

All jobs moved to `aws-m8i-8xl-cache` (128 GiB). The 2xl runner was insufficient for two reasons:

title: Fix dtype mismatch in grouped_mm_fallback for LoRA training on Mamba+…
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47933)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47933)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

…MoE models

Ensure tensor dtype consistency in matrix multiplications.

## What does this PR do?
 
Fixes a `RuntimeError` when fine-tuning hybrid Mamba+MoE models (e.g. `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`) with LoRA using `SFTTrainer`.
 
**Problem:** `torch.amp.autocast` produces `float32` activations and gradients, while the MoE model weights are `bfloat16`. The `_grouped_mm_fallback` kernel does not handle mixed dtypes in the forward or backward pass, causing:
 
```
RuntimeError: expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype, but got: float != c10::BFloat16
```
 
**Fix:** Cast input/output tensors to match the weight tensor dtype at the point of the matmul in both `_grouped_mm_fallback` (forward) and `_grouped_mm_fallback_backward` (backward).
 
The cast uses `.to(weight[i].dtype)` / `.to(grad_weight[i].dtype)` — fully dynamic, adapts to any dtype, and is a no-op when dtypes already match.
 
## Tested on
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16` (Mamba-2 + MoE + Attention hybrid)
- Method: LoRA SFT using HuggingFace TRL `SFTTrainer`
- Hardware: NVIDIA H100 PCIe 80 GB
- transformers: `5.16.0.dev0`

title: Speculative decoding: candidate generators return a `q` they did not sample from, breaking losslessness with `do_sample=True`
body:
### System Info

```
transformers version: 5.16.0.dev0 (source checkout at main, d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e)
Platform: macOS-26.4.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
Python version: 3.14.6
PyTorch version: 2.11.0
Accelerator: CPU for the first two scripts; the real-checkpoint run used one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB
```

### Who can help?

@Cyrilvallez

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [X] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [X] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

`_speculative_sampling` treats the `candidate_logits` returned by a candidate generator as `q`, the drafter's
proposal distribution. Three of the block drafters return logits that are not the distribution their tokens were
drawn from, so with `do_sample=True` the acceptance test is run against the wrong `q`.

#### The mismatch

In `DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator.get_candidates`, each token is sampled from the **processor-applied** logits
([`candidate_generator.py#L1674-L1685`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py#L1674-L1685)):

```python
if self.logits_processor is not None:
    candidate_ids = input_ids
    for i in range(candidate_logits.shape[1]):
        next_token_logits = self.logits_processor(candidate_ids, candidate_logits[:, i, :].float())
        if self.do_sample:
            probs = nn.functional.softmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1, dtype=torch.float32)
            next_token = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1)
```

but the method returns the **raw** `candidate_logits`
([`#L1696`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py#L1696)).
`next_token_logits` is discarded.

Those returned logits then become `q` in
[`_speculative_sampling`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L3992-L4063),
which uses them for the acceptance ratio
([`utils.py#L4013-L4022`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L4013-L4022))
and for the `[p - q]+` residual it samples from on rejection
([`#L4045`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L4045)).

With a top-k warper the drafter samples from `q(x)/Z` (`Z` = raw mass kept by the warper) but reports `q(x)`, so
`p_i/q_i` is computed a factor `1/Z` too large and draft tokens are accepted more often than the algorithm allows.

#### Reproduction

The drafter's vocab projection is pinned to a fixed logits vector, so its raw distribution is known exactly and
every drafted position is an i.i.d. draw from it. This measures what the drafter actually draws and compares it
with what it hands back.

```python
"""Shows that DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator returns logits that are not the distribution it sampled from.

Run against transformers main. The drafter's vocab projection is pinned to a fixed
logits vector, so the drafter's raw distribution is known exactly and every drafted
position is an i.i.d. draw from it.
"""

import torch
from torch import nn

from transformers import GenerationConfig
from transformers.generation.candidate_generator import DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator
from transformers.generation.logits_process import LogitsProcessorList, TopKLogitsWarper
from transformers.models.muse_glimmer_assistant import (
    MuseGlimmerAssistantConfig,
    MuseGlimmerAssistantModel,
)
from transformers.modeling_outputs import BaseModelOutputWithPast

VOCAB_SIZE = 8
HIDDEN_SIZE = 32
BLOCK_SIZE = 8
PROMPT_LENGTH = 6
TOP_K = 3

# The drafter's raw next-token logits, identical at every drafted position.
RAW_LOGITS = torch.tensor([3.0, 2.6, 2.2, 1.0, 0.6, 0.2, 0.0, -0.4])


class PinnedOutputEmbeddings(nn.Module):
    """Stands in for the main model's LM head, so the drafter's distribution is fixed and known."""

    def forward(self, hidden_states):
        logits = RAW_LOGITS.to(hidden_states.device).expand(*hidden_states.shape[:2], VOCAB_SIZE)
        return logits.clone()


def build_inputs():
    config = MuseGlimmerAssistantConfig(
        vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE,
        hidden_size=HIDDEN_SIZE,
        head_dim=8,
        num_hidden_layers=3,
        num_attention_heads=4,
        num_key_value_heads=2,
        intermediate_size=37,
        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
        target_layer_ids=[0, 2],
        mask_token_id=1,
        bos_token_id=2,
        eos_token_id=3,
        pad_token_id=4,
    )
    assistant_model = MuseGlimmerAssistantModel(config).eval()
    input_embeddings = nn.Embedding(VOCAB_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE)
    input_ids = torch.zeros(1, PROMPT_LENGTH, dtype=torch.long)
    model_kwargs = {
        "position_ids": torch.arange(PROMPT_LENGTH)[None],
        "attention_mask": torch.ones(1, PROMPT_LENGTH, dtype=torch.long),
    }
    model_outputs = BaseModelOutputWithPast(
        last_hidden_state=torch.randn(1, PROMPT_LENGTH, HIDDEN_SIZE),
        hidden_states=tuple(torch.randn(1, PROMPT_LENGTH, HIDDEN_SIZE) for _ in range(4)),
    )
    return assistant_model, input_embeddings, input_ids, model_kwargs, model_outputs


def draft_once(assistant_model, input_embeddings, input_ids, model_kwargs, model_outputs):
    """One fresh drafting round; returns the drafted tokens and the logits handed back to the caller."""
    generation_config = GenerationConfig(do_sample=True, top_k=TOP_K, max_length=1024)
    candidate_generator = DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator(
        assistant_model=assistant_model,
        main_model_input_embeddings=input_embeddings,
        main_model_output_embeddings=PinnedOutputEmbeddings(),
        generation_config=generation_config,
        # exactly what `generate()` hands the drafter for `do_sample=True, top_k=3`
        logits_processor=LogitsProcessorList([TopKLogitsWarper(top_k=TOP_K)]),
    )
    candidate_ids, candidate_logits = candidate_generator.get_candidates(
        input_ids=input_ids,
        model_kwargs=model_kwargs,
        model_outputs=model_outputs,
        is_first_iteration=False,
        n_last_matches=0,
    )
    return candidate_ids[0, PROMPT_LENGTH:], candidate_logits


def main():
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    assistant_model, input_embeddings, input_ids, model_kwargs, model_outputs = build_inputs()

    counts = torch.zeros(VOCAB_SIZE)
    returned_logits = None
    rounds = 600
    for _ in range(rounds):
        drafted, candidate_logits = draft_once(
            assistant_model, input_embeddings, input_ids, model_kwargs, model_outputs
        )
        counts += torch.bincount(drafted, minlength=VOCAB_SIZE)
        returned_logits = candidate_logits

    empirical = counts / counts.sum()

    # `_speculative_sampling` reads the returned logits as q.
    q_returned = returned_logits[0, 0].softmax(dim=-1)

    # What the drafter actually sampled from: top-k applied, then renormalised.
    q_actual = TopKLogitsWarper(top_k=TOP_K)(input_ids, RAW_LOGITS[None].clone()).softmax(dim=-1)[0]

    kept = q_actual > 0
    Z = q_returned[kept].sum()

    print(f"transformers: {__import__('transformers').__version__}")
    print(f"draws: {int(counts.sum())} over {rounds} drafting rounds, top_k={TOP_K}\n")
    print("token   q returned (raw)   q sampled from   empirical")
    for token in range(VOCAB_SIZE):
        print(f"{token:>5}   {q_returned[token]:>16.4f}   {q_actual[token]:>14.4f}   {empirical[token]:>9.4f}")

    print(f"\nmass the returned q puts on the tokens the drafter can actually draw: Z = {Z:.4f}")
    print(f"acceptance ratio p/q is therefore inflated by 1/Z = {1 / Z:.4f}x for every accepted token")

    max_dev_returned = (empirical - q_returned).abs().max()
    max_dev_actual = (empirical - q_actual).abs().max()
    print(f"\nmax |empirical - q returned| = {max_dev_returned:.4f}")
    print(f"max |empirical - q sampled from| = {max_dev_actual:.4f}")

    unreachable = (~kept) & (q_returned > 0.01)
    print(
        f"tokens the returned q gives >1% but the drafter never proposes: "
        f"{unreachable.nonzero().flatten().tolist()}"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Output:

```
transformers: 5.16.0.dev0
draws: 4200 over 600 drafting rounds, top_k=3

token   q returned (raw)   q sampled from   empirical
    0             0.4017           0.4718      0.4707
    1             0.2692           0.3162      0.3093
    2             0.1805           0.2120      0.2200
    3             0.0544           0.0000      0.0000
    4             0.0364           0.0000      0.0000
    5             0.0244           0.0000      0.0000
    6             0.0200           0.0000      0.0000
    7             0.0134           0.0000      0.0000

mass the returned q puts on the tokens the drafter can actually draw: Z = 0.8514
acceptance ratio p/q is therefore inflated by 1/Z = 1.1746x for every accepted token

max |empirical - q returned| = 0.0691
max |empirical - q sampled from| = 0.0080
tokens the returned q gives >1% but the drafter never proposes: [3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
```

The drafted tokens track the processed distribution, not the returned one. The returned `q` also puts 15% of its
mass on five tokens the drafter can never propose, which is the mass the `[p - q]+` residual is built from.

#### What that costs, on real models at the real defaults

There is no small DFlash checkpoint published, so the section above pins a synthetic head to get a known
drafter distribution. To get the magnitude on real distributions, this takes a real drafter and a real target,
substitutes `q` exactly the way the drafters above do, and runs the library's own `_speculative_sampling`.

`Z` is the quantity that sets the error: the raw mass sitting on the tokens `top_k=50` keeps. The committed-token
distribution is computed in closed form and cross-checked against the library's verifier at the end of the run.

<details>
<summary>Script</summary>

```python
"""Measures the mismatch on real models, at the sampling defaults `generate()` actually uses.

`top_k` defaults to 50, so a drafter over a 49k-token vocabulary proposes from a renormalised
distribution whose raw mass is Z. This measures Z on a real drafter, then measures what reporting
the un-renormalised distribution as `q` does to the committed-token distribution.

The committed distribution is computed in closed form and cross-checked against the library's own
`_speculative_sampling` on a subset of positions.
"""

import torch

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.generation.logits_process import TopKLogitsWarper
from transformers.generation.utils import _speculative_sampling

DRAFTER = "HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M"
TARGET = "HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M"
TOP_K = 50  # the `generate()` default for do_sample=True
POSITIONS = 400  # real next-token distributions to measure
MC_POSITIONS = 6  # positions to cross-check against the library's verifier
MC_DRAWS = 20_000

PROMPTS = [
    "The main difference between a hash table and a balanced tree is",
    "When the rain finally stopped, the streets outside were",
    "To install the package on a fresh machine, first",
    "She had never seen the ocean before, and her first thought was",
    "The committee met for three hours and eventually decided that",
    "In a distributed system, consensus is hard because",
    "He opened the letter slowly, already knowing what it would",
    "The recipe calls for butter, but you can substitute",
]


def collect_real_distributions(drafter, target, tokenizer):
    """Runs the drafter forward on real text and returns aligned (raw drafter, target) logits."""
    warper = TopKLogitsWarper(top_k=TOP_K)
    rows = []
    for prompt in PROMPTS:
        input_ids = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").input_ids
        # Let the drafter extend its own text, so the contexts are the kind it actually drafts from
        with torch.no_grad():
            input_ids = drafter.generate(
                input_ids,
                do_sample=True,
                top_k=TOP_K,
                max_new_tokens=POSITIONS // len(PROMPTS),
                pad_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
            )
            drafter_logits = drafter(input_ids).logits[0].float()
            target_logits = target(input_ids).logits[0].float()
        for position in range(input_ids.shape[1] - 1):
            context = input_ids[:, : position + 1]
            q_raw = drafter_logits[position]
            # what the drafter samples from, and what the verifier compares against
            q_processed = warper(context, q_raw[None].clone())[0]
            p_processed = warper(context, target_logits[position][None].clone())[0]
            rows.append((q_raw, q_processed, p_processed, context.shape[1]))
    return rows


def committed_distribution(p, q_reported, q_actual):
    """Closed form of what `_speculative_sampling` commits at position 0, for candidate_length=1."""
    # `is_accepted = r_i <= probability_ratio` with r_i ~ U(0,1), so acceptance is min(1, p/q_reported)
    ratio = torch.where(q_reported > 0, p / q_reported.clamp_min(torch.finfo(p.dtype).tiny), torch.zeros_like(p))
    accept_prob = ratio.clamp(max=1.0)
    committed = q_actual * accept_prob
    reject_mass = 1.0 - committed.sum()

    residual = (p - q_reported).clamp(min=0)
    residual_sum = residual.sum()
    if residual_sum > 0:
        residual = residual / residual_sum
    return committed + reject_mass * residual, committed.sum()


def monte_carlo_committed(p_logits, q_reported_logits, q_actual_probs, draws):
    """Same quantity, but measured through the library's own verifier."""
    counts = torch.zeros(p_logits.shape[-1])
    new_logits = torch.stack([p_logits, p_logits])[None]
    candidate_logits = q_reported_logits[None, None]
    drafted = torch.multinomial(q_actual_probs, num_samples=draws, replacement=True)
    for i in range(draws):
        candidate_input_ids = torch.tensor([[0, drafted[i]]])
        valid_tokens, _ = _speculative_sampling(
            candidate_input_ids, candidate_logits, 1, new_logits, is_done_candidate=False
        )
        counts[valid_tokens[0, 0]] += 1
    return counts / counts.sum()


def quantiles(values, points=(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95)):
    tensor = torch.tensor(values)
    return {point: torch.quantile(tensor, point).item() for point in points}


def main():
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(DRAFTER)
    drafter = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(DRAFTER, dtype=torch.float32).eval()
    target = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(TARGET, dtype=torch.float32).eval()

    rows = collect_real_distributions(drafter, target, tokenizer)

    z_values, tv_raw, tv_processed, accept_raw, accept_processed, ctx_lens = [], [], [], [], [], []
    for q_raw, q_processed, p_processed, ctx_len in rows:
        q_raw_probs = q_raw.softmax(dim=-1)
        q_actual = q_processed.softmax(dim=-1)
        p = p_processed.softmax(dim=-1)

        # Z: the raw mass sitting on the tokens the warper kept
        z = q_raw_probs[q_actual > 0].sum().item()
        z_values.append(z)

        buggy, accepted_buggy = committed_distribution(p, q_raw_probs, q_actual)
        fixed, accepted_fixed = committed_distribution(p, q_actual, q_actual)
        tv_raw.append(0.5 * (buggy - p).abs().sum().item())
        tv_processed.append(0.5 * (fixed - p).abs().sum().item())
        accept_raw.append(accepted_buggy.item())
        accept_processed.append(accepted_fixed.item())
        ctx_lens.append(ctx_len)

    print(f"transformers: {__import__('transformers').__version__}")
    print(f"drafter: {DRAFTER}  target: {TARGET}  vocab: {drafter.config.vocab_size}")
    print(f"top_k={TOP_K} (the `generate()` default), {len(rows)} real next-token positions")

    # Very short contexts are high-entropy, so they strip the most mass and flatter the result.
    # Reported separately rather than pooled, since real drafting happens after a real prompt.
    for label, keep in (
        ("all positions", lambda i: True),
        (">= 8 tokens of context", lambda i: ctx_lens[i] >= 8),
    ):
        index = [i for i in range(len(rows)) if keep(i)]
        z_subset = [z_values[i] for i in index]
        tv_subset = [tv_raw[i] for i in index]
        inflation = [1.0 / z_values[i] for i in index]

        zq, iq, tvq = quantiles(z_subset), quantiles(inflation), quantiles(tv_subset)
        print(f"\n=== {label} (n={len(index)}) ===")
        print("Z, the raw mass on the tokens top_k=50 keeps:")
        print(
            f"  p05 {zq[0.05]:.4f}   p25 {zq[0.25]:.4f}   median {zq[0.5]:.4f}   "
            f"p75 {zq[0.75]:.4f}   p95 {zq[0.95]:.4f}"
        )
        print("acceptance-ratio inflation 1/Z:")
        print(
            f"  p05 {iq[0.05]:.4f}   p25 {iq[0.25]:.4f}   median {iq[0.5]:.4f}   "
            f"p75 {iq[0.75]:.4f}   p95 {iq[0.95]:.4f}   worst {max(inflation):.4f}x"
        )
        print("total variation between committed tokens and the target, q raw (as on main):")
        print(
            f"  p05 {tvq[0.05]:.4f}   p25 {tvq[0.25]:.4f}   median {tvq[0.5]:.4f}   "
            f"p75 {tvq[0.75]:.4f}   p95 {tvq[0.95]:.4f}   worst {max(tv_subset):.4f}"
        )
        print(f"  same quantity with q processed (control): max {max(tv_processed[i] for i in index):.2e}")
        print(f"mean draft acceptance rate, q raw (as on main): {sum(accept_raw[i] for i in index) / len(index):.4f}")
        print(
            f"mean draft acceptance rate, q processed:        "
            f"{sum(accept_processed[i] for i in index) / len(index):.4f}",
            flush=True,
        )
    print(flush=True)

    # Cross-check the closed form against the library's verifier on the positions where it matters most.
    # Without this the numbers above would only be my model of the code, not the code.
    print(
        f"closed form vs library `_speculative_sampling`, {MC_POSITIONS} worst positions x {MC_DRAWS} draws",
        flush=True,
    )
    print("  position   TV(analytic)   TV(measured)   |analytic - measured|", flush=True)
    long_context = [i for i in range(len(rows)) if ctx_lens[i] >= 8]
    worst = sorted(long_context, key=lambda i: -tv_raw[i])[:MC_POSITIONS]
    deviations = []
    for index in worst:
        q_raw, q_processed, p_processed, _ = rows[index]
        q_actual = q_processed.softmax(dim=-1)
        p = p_processed.softmax(dim=-1)
        analytic, _ = committed_distribution(p, q_raw.softmax(dim=-1), q_actual)
        measured = monte_carlo_committed(p_processed, q_raw, q_actual, MC_DRAWS)
        deviation = 0.5 * (analytic - measured).abs().sum().item()
        deviations.append(deviation)
        print(
            f"  {index:>8}   {tv_raw[index]:>12.4f}   {0.5 * (measured - p).abs().sum().item():>12.4f}   "
            f"{deviation:>21.4f}",
            flush=True,
        )
    print(f"\n  max |closed form - library| = {max(deviations):.4f} (Monte Carlo noise floor at this draw count)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Reading the `>= 8 tokens of context` block, which is the representative one — very short contexts are
high-entropy, so they strip the most mass and overstate the effect, and both populations are reported rather than
pooled for that reason. The drafter proposes from a distribution whose raw mass is a median of `0.89`, so `p/q` is
computed a median of `1.12x` too large, `1.84x` at p95, and `3.02x` at the worst position (`7.76x` if the
one-token contexts are included). The committed tokens sit a median total variation of `0.045` from the target
distribution and `0.168` at p95, and draft acceptance runs at `0.779` where the algorithm allows `0.730`.

The last block is the control that makes those numbers mean anything: passing the processed logits as `q` puts
the committed distribution within `1.85e-07` of the target, and the closed form agrees with the library's actual
verifier to within Monte Carlo noise at 20k draws. The deviation is the substituted `q`, not the measurement.

#### Confirmed on the real DFlash checkpoints

Run on an NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB with `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` + `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-assistant` in bf16, transformers `5.16.0.dev0` at the pinned
commit. `generate(assistant_model=..., speculation_type="dflash", do_sample=True)` ran end to end and produced
coherent text, so this is the real generator on real weights.

The sampling settings are the model's own shipped ones (`{"do_sample": true, "top_k": 64, "top_p": 0.95, "temperature": 1.0}`), which `generate()` turns into `TopKLogitsWarper`, `TopPLogitsWarper`. For each
prompt the first drafted token was sampled 3000 times from a fixed drafter state, and the
empirical distribution compared against the two candidates for `q`.

| prompt | Z | 1/Z | drafter support | TV vs **returned** q | TV vs **sampled** q | mass q gives unreachable tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `The main difference between a hash…` | 0.9386 | 1.065x | 8 | 0.0655 | **0.0141** | 0.0614 |
| `When the rain finally stopped, the…` | 0.8221 | 1.216x | 52 | 0.1863 | **0.0432** | 0.1779 |
| `To install the package on a fresh …` | 0.9013 | 1.110x | 27 | 0.1067 | **0.0228** | 0.0987 |
| `She had never seen the ocean befor…` | 0.9099 | 1.099x | 19 | 0.0960 | **0.0176** | 0.0901 |

In every prompt the drafted tokens track the distribution the drafter sampled from, not the one it returned — the
returned `q` is off by 4x to 5x more in total variation. Note the support column: `top_p=0.95` collapses a
202048-token vocabulary to between 8 and 52 candidates, and the returned `q` spreads 6-18% of its mass over tokens
the drafter cannot propose at all. That mass is what the `[p - q]+` residual is built from on rejection.

### Expected behavior

`generate()` should sample from the target model's distribution regardless of whether speculative decoding is
enabled. `assistant_ensemble_weight` documents this as the property you opt out of
([`configuration_utils.py#L354-L359`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py#L354-L359)):

> Defaults to `None`, which keeps decoding lossless.

With `assistant_ensemble_weight=None` and the drafters below, decoding is not lossless.

#### Affected generators

| Generator | Samples from | Returns as `q` | Affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator` | processor-applied logits ([`#L1678-L1685`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py#L1678-L1685)) | raw logits ([`#L1696`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py#L1696)) | yes |
| `MTPCandidateGenerator` → `MtpModel.forward` | processor-applied logits ([`modeling_layers.py#L540-L546`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/modeling_layers.py#L540-L546)) | raw logits ([`#L537`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/modeling_layers.py#L537), returned at [`#L558-L560`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/modeling_layers.py#L558-L560)) | yes, same shape |
| `SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator` | `outputs.logits.argmax`, no processors, regardless of `do_sample` ([`#L1388`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py#L1388)) | raw logits ([`#L1414-L1415`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py#L1414-L1415)) | yes, differently |

`SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator` deviates further: it accepts a `logits_processor` and the parent
stores it ([`#L171`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py#L171)),
but `get_candidates` never reads it and never samples — the draft is deterministic even with `do_sample=True`. Its
returned logits are at least the ones the argmax was taken over, but the true proposal is a point mass on that
argmax, so `q_i` is again smaller than the probability the token was actually proposed with. If greedy drafting is
intended there, the returned logits still do not describe the proposal.

I verified the DFlash path empirically (above) and the other two by reading; I did not run MTP or
`SinglePosition` end to end.

#### Reachability

All three receive the target's `logits_processor` from `_get_candidate_generator`
([MTP `#L1035-L1041`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L1035-L1041),
[SinglePosition `#L1055-L1063`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L1055-L1063),
[DFlash `#L1064-L1071`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L1064-L1071)),
so DFlash and MTP always take the processor branch, and `_assisted_decoding` routes to `_speculative_sampling`
whenever `do_sample=True` and the generator returned logits
([`#L3744-L3752`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L3744-L3752)).
Nothing gates `do_sample` against `speculation_type="dflash"` or `use_mtp`.

An empty `LogitsProcessorList` is identity, so the mismatch needs at least one non-identity processor. With
`do_sample=True` that is the default: `top_k` defaults to `50`, which appends a `TopKLogitsWarper`
([`#L1315-L1318`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L1315-L1318)).

It is also the shipped default for the DFlash model itself, so this does not need an unusual configuration.
[`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/generation_config.json`](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/blob/main/generation_config.json)
ships `"do_sample": true, "top_k": 64, "top_p": 0.95`, and with that config `_get_logits_processor` builds:

```python
>>> gc = GenerationConfig.from_pretrained("meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B")
>>> gc.update(**gc._get_default_generation_params(), defaults_only=True)
>>> {"do_sample": gc.do_sample, "top_k": gc.top_k, "top_p": gc.top_p, "temperature": gc.temperature}
{'do_sample': True, 'top_k': 64, 'top_p': 0.95, 'temperature': 1.0}
>>> [type(p).__name__ for p in model._get_logits_processor(generation_config=gc, ...)]
['TopKLogitsWarper', 'TopPLogitsWarper']
```

Two non-identity warpers, on a 202048-token vocabulary, on the checkpoint the DFlash generator was added for.

#### Why the existing guard does not catch it

There is already a test for exactly this property —
[`test_speculative_sampling_target_distribution`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/tests/generation/test_utils.py#L2979-L3029),
added in #34553 to prevent issues like #32867. It cannot catch this, by construction: it calls
`_speculative_sampling` directly with hand-written `candidate_logits`, so `q` is the distribution the draft came
from *by assumption*. The bug is in the contract between the generator and the verifier, and the test never runs a
generator.

Nothing else covers that contract either. `tests/generation/test_candidate_generator.py` has three test classes on
main (`TestAssistantToTargetTranslator`, `TestAssistantVocabTranslatorCache`, `TestUniversalSpeculativeDecoding`)
and none for DFlash or MTP. The MuseGlimmer assistant model tests are
[skipped](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/tests/models/muse_glimmer_assistant/test_modeling_muse_glimmer_assistant.py#L113)
with *"Need some test work, as it needs different inputs (dflash speculator model)"*, and `test_generate_with_mtp`
checks that `mtp.*` weights reload, not that the drafts are distributed correctly.

The gap a regression test would need to close: assert that the logits a generator returns describe the
distribution its tokens were actually drawn from. The first script above is one shape that does it.

#### Relationship to open work

Checked so this is not a duplicate:

- #47913 (open, DFlash selective hidden-state capture and TP sharding) touches `candidate_generator.py`, but its
  diff does not change the sampling block or the return — different concern.
- #47877 (open) fixes a DFlash device mismatch under `device_map="auto"`; unrelated.
- #47931 (open) crops DFlash drafts at the first EOS. Same method, different defect: that one is about *which*
  drafted tokens are committed, this one is about *which distribution* they were drawn from. Neither fixes
  the other, and this defect predates it.
- #45979 (merged) added `assistant_ensemble_weight` and the "keeps decoding lossless" wording this report relies on.

I did not find an existing issue or PR for the mismatch itself.

#### Severity, stated honestly

Nothing crashes and the output is still fluent text — this is a silent distribution shift, and only with
`do_sample=True`. Greedy assisted decoding is unaffected: it does not go through `_speculative_sampling`, and it
keeps draft tokens only where they equal the target's own argmax
([`#L3771-L3779`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d1123114da1ab4395198146f4f84dae7fe8b693e/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L3771-L3779)),
so the committed tokens are the target's greedy output whatever the drafter proposed.

What I have and have not shown. The DFlash mismatch is confirmed on the real checkpoints, at the model's own
shipped sampling settings, on four prompts x 3000 draws each. The SmolLM2 section is a different claim: it puts a
number on what the substituted `q` costs the *committed* distribution, which needs a target and a drafter I can
run many thousands of verifier rounds against. `Z` depends on the model, the sampling parameters and the position,
so other pairs and settings will land elsewhere — a `top_k` large enough to keep essentially all the mass makes
the error vanish, and a smaller `top_k`/`top_p` or a `temperature` above 1 makes it worse.

Two gaps I did not close. I did not measure the end-to-end committed-token distribution on Muse-Glimmer itself —
that needs enough verifier rounds to resolve a distribution over a 202048-token vocabulary, which is a much longer
run than the one above. And I did not run MTP or `SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator` at all; those two
are reported from reading the code, and the table above should not be read as covering them.

I have not opened a PR — CONTRIBUTING asks to coordinate on an issue first, and the right fix depends on whether
the processed logits should be returned or the drafter should stop applying processors. Happy to submit one if
that would help.

title: Crop DFlash drafts at the first EOS
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47931)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47931)

# Crop DFlash drafts at the first EOS

Fixes #47912.

Per @zucchini-nlp's [review](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/47912#issuecomment-5264064690),
this puts the fix inside `DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator.get_candidates` rather than in
`_assisted_decoding`, mirroring what `PromptLookupCandidateGenerator` already does to its drafts
(`candidate_generator.py:1129`).

## The bug

`_assisted_decoding` commits `n_matches + 1` tokens per round. It appends and streams the whole block
*before* running the stopping criteria, and `EosTokenCriteria` only inspects the last `new_token_length=1`
tokens. So an EOS accepted anywhere but the end of a committed block is missed and generation runs past it.
It looks intermittent because an EOS that happens to land on the bonus token stops correctly.

Block proposers hit this routinely — DFlash drafts `block_size` (16 for the shipped drafter) at a time.
Classic autoregressive drafters mostly avoid it because their draft stops at EOS, leaving it last.

## Why cropping the draft is sufficient

`n_matches` is the length of the leading run where the target model's argmax equals the drafted token
(`utils.py:3774`), and `valid_tokens = selected_tokens[:, : n_matches + 1]` (`:3779`). So every committed
position before the last one is provably a drafted token, and only the final one — the correction/bonus
token — can be an EOS that was not in the draft. That one is already fine: it lands last, so the criteria
fire. Cropping the draft at its first EOS therefore makes an EOS-before-the-end impossible.

When the whole cropped draft is accepted, the existing guard at `:3777` (`is_done_candidate and
n_matches == candidate_length`) decrements `n_matches`, dropping the bonus token and leaving EOS last.
The same argument covers sampling: `_speculative_sampling` builds `valid_tokens` from the drafted tokens
plus a resampled correction and has its own equivalent guard at `:4032`.

Note the gating is exact: `EosTokenCriteria` is installed iff `generation_config._eos_token_tensor is not
None` (`utils.py:1383-1384`), and this crop fires on that same tensor. The crop and the stopping criterion
are driven by precisely the same token set, so a block can never be shortened for a token that would not
have stopped generation. That is also why it reads `_eos_token_tensor` rather than following the
`SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator` idiom of unioning the assistant's `eos_token_id` — that union
can contain ids the criteria ignore.

Cropping rather than pad-and-zero (what `SinglePosition` does) because DFlash is batch-1 by construction
(`candidate_generator.py:1588`, `:1656`), consistent with the existing note next to the prompt-lookup crop
that "assisted decoding supports only bs=1". So there is no ragged-batch case to pad around, and a shorter
block also skips verifying tokens that are known-dead.

The assistant's own cache is unaffected: it always forwards the full `block_size` noise window before the
crop, and `cache.crop(-self.block_size)` / `set_previous_accepted_tokens(...)` are driven by `block_size`
and `n_matches`, never by how many candidates were returned.

## Verification on the real model

Ran on the real pair — `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` + `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-assistant`, bf16 on
one A100 80GB, greedy, `max_new_tokens=512`, `block_size=16`. Both arms are the same machine and the same
weights with only `git apply` between them. "past EOS" counts tokens committed after the first EOS:

| prompt | plain greedy | `speculation_type="dflash"` before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `List the first eight prime numbers…` | 184 tok, EOS@183 | 191 tok, **+21 past EOS** | 170 tok, +0 |
| `Name the four cardinal directions…` | 222 tok, EOS@221 | 296 tok, **+74 past EOS** | 222 tok, +0 |
| `Reply with exactly the word: done` | 94 tok, EOS@93 | 396 tok, **+302 past EOS** | 94 tok, +0 |
| `Count from 1 to 5…` | 255 tok, EOS@254 | 211 tok, **+15 past EOS** | 196 tok, +0 |
| `What is 2+2? Answer with just the number.` | 90 tok, EOS@89 | 494 tok, **+404 past EOS** | 90 tok, +0 |
| `List three primary colours…` | 374 tok, EOS@373 | 367 tok, +0 | 367 tok, +0 |

5 of 6 prompts ran past an accepted EOS before the change and 0 of 6 after; every prompt reached an EOS,
so none is inconclusive. As a positive control that the new code is what did it, the drafter was
instrumented to record every block: **0 short blocks across all 6 unpatched runs, 7 across the patched
runs** — the crop fires exactly when the drafter proposes an EOS and never otherwise. Across ~720 recorded
blocks the returned `candidate_logits` length matched the drafted-token count every time.

One thing worth stating plainly, because it is easy to assume otherwise: dflash output is **not** token-for-token
identical to plain greedy here, and was not before this change either (0/6 exact matches before, 3/6 after).
Verifying a 16-token block and decoding one token at a time use different kernel shapes, so bf16 rounding
differs and an argmax can flip. That is orthogonal to this fix and predates it — which is why the criterion
above is "commits nothing after an accepted EOS" rather than "equals greedy".

New tests in `tests/generation/test_candidate_generator.py` build a tiny `MuseGlimmerAssistantModel` and a
real `DFlashCache`, pinning only the vocab projection so the drafted block is deterministic. They cover
cropping at the first of several EOS, no EOS, EOS already last, and a leading EOS; the logits are asserted
to track the tokens positionally (`argmax`), not merely to match in length. Reverting only the
`candidate_generator.py` change fails the crop tests while the "untouched" ones keep passing.

`tests/generation/test_utils.py` and `test_stopping_criteria.py` show the same failures by name before and
after this change in my environment (network-dependent tests).

## Scope

This fixes DFlash only, as requested. **`MTPCandidateGenerator` still has the same defect** — its
`get_candidates` ends with a bare `torch.cat` and no EOS crop (`candidate_generator.py:1537`) — and #47912
names MTP as affected. Happy to extend this PR to MTP, or leave it for a follow-up, whichever you prefer.

Separately and pre-existing, not touched here: DFlash samples from processor-applied logits
(`:1678-1684`) but returns the raw `candidate_logits`, so `_speculative_sampling` computes the acceptance
ratio against a distribution the drafter did not sample from. I can open a separate issue.

---

*AI-assisted contribution, per CONTRIBUTING.md: drafted with Claude Code; the results above are from
actual runs, and I have reviewed the changed lines and the behaviour before submitting.*

title: Add support for Lumma Model
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47929)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47929)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## PR Overview

This PR adds native support for the Lumma AI model to the transformers library, allowing users to load and run Lumma through the standard `from_pretrained(...)` API without requiring custom remote code.

Lumma by FrontiersMind is a Llama-style decoder with efficiency-oriented architectural choices - factorized embeddings, GQA, optional layer sharing, shared KV attention, and configurable Q/QK normalization.

### Architecture
  - Factorized embeddings to reduce the size of the embedding layers.
  - Grouped Query Attention (GQA) for more efficient attention.
  - Shared KV attention, where the value projection is reused from the key projection.
  - Q-norm / QK-norm support for normalizing queries and keys.
  - Optional layer sharing, allowing the same layers to be reused multiple times.
  - RoPE and Llama-style MLP, keeping the familiar Llama architecture.

I would really appreciate it if you could take a look at this PR and share any feedback or suggestions. We’re hoping to get this merged soon, so please let me know if there’s anything that needs to be addressed before merging. We’ll be happy to make the necessary changes promptly.

title: Continuous batching auto-switches to flash_attention_3 on unsupported GPUs (Turing/T4), crashing — regression from 5.14.1
body:
### System Info

- Affected: `transformers==5.15.0` (also current `main` / `5.16.0.dev0`). **Not** reproduced on the `v5.14.1` release.
- Same environment also moved `kernels==0.15.2` → `kernels==0.16.0`, and the `kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3` Hub kernel is now pulled.
- GPU: NVIDIA **T4** (Turing, SM 7.5), i.e. **pre-Ampere**. `flash_attn` is not pip-installed (only `transformers[kernels]`).
- Container: `pytorch/pytorch:2.8.0-cuda12.8-cudnn9-devel`.

### Who can help?

cc @remi-or @IlyasMoutawwakil (continuous batching)

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

Running generation with continuous batching (`generate_batch` / `use_transformers_continuous_batching=True`) on a **pre-Ampere** GPU (NVIDIA T4).

On `5.15.0`, continuous batching auto-switches the attention implementation from `sdpa` to `flash_attention_3` and loads the `kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3` Hub kernel:

```
ContinuousBatchingLogger - WARNING - Continuous batching is much better when using flash attention. Switching from sdpa to flash_attention_3. If you need to use eager or sdpa, use paged|eager or paged|sdpa as the `attn_implementation`.
transformers.modeling_utils - WARNING - You do not have `flash_attn` installed, using `paged|kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3` from the `kernels` library instead!
```

The generation loop then crashes, because that kernel requires newer hardware:

```
ContinuousBatchingLogger - ERROR - Error in generation loop: mha_fwd, /build/source/flash-attn/flash_api_stable.cpp:716, FlashAttention only supports Ampere GPUs or newer.
ContinuousBatchingLogger - ERROR - Generation thread terminated unexpectedly.
ContinuousBatchingLogger - ERROR - Requests ['req_0', 'req_1', 'req_2'] not found in results.
```

Because the generation thread dies, no completions are returned, which then breaks downstream code that assumes at least one completion.

The same code runs fine on `v5.14.1` (with `kernels==0.15.2`): continuous batching does **not** switch to `flash_attention_3`, and generation completes normally.

Observed in CI on a single-GPU T4 runner (downstream project TRL):
- Passing: `transformers==5.14.1` / `kernels==0.15.2` — https://github.com/huggingface/trl/actions/runs/31371150907/job/93400203818
- Failing: `transformers==5.15.0` / `kernels==0.16.0` — https://github.com/huggingface/trl/actions/runs/31582787840/job/94069521759

Workaround: pass `attn_implementation="paged|sdpa"` (or `paged|eager`).

### Expected behavior

Continuous batching should not switch to `flash_attention_3` on GPUs that cannot run it. The auto-switch should be gated on device capability (or fall back to `sdpa`) instead of hard-crashing the generation thread, as was the case on `v5.14.1`.

> Note: I don't yet have a minimal non-CI reproduction on non-Ampere hardware; the above is from CI logs plus a version bisect (`model_runner.py` is byte-identical between `v5.14.1` and `v5.15.0`, so the change is in the attention/kernel default selection). I'll add the exact regressing change — and whether it originates in `transformers` or in the `kernels` default resolution — as a follow-up once pinned.

title: Keep MXFP4 weights quantized on XPU when use_kernels is set
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47923)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47923)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

`Mxfp4HfQuantizer` dequantizes to bf16 whenever `use_kernels` is set on any
accelerator other than CPU, because kernel layers were assumed to need dense
weights. That no longer holds on XPU: the `megablocks` layer already mapped to
XPU for `MegaBlocksMoeMLP` reads MXFP4 experts natively. This adds `xpu` to the
same allow-list CPU is already on.

## Why

Dequantizing inflates the expert weights ~3.8x, and every MoE forward then
re-reads that inflated tensor on a path that is already bandwidth-bound.

Measured on GPT-OSS with Intel Arc Pro B60, `torch 2.13.0+xpu`: quantized, the
model fits on a single card; dequantized, it has to be spread across several,
and is still slower end to end. Generated output is unchanged.

## Dependencies

Requires the `megablocks` change that teaches the XPU layer to read the triton
MXFP4 representation, and a `megablocks` build carrying it published on the Hub.
Until then the XPU layer would receive weights it cannot interpret.

title: Fix CLIP _init_weights when a child module carries quantized weights
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47921)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47921)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #47920

`CLIPPreTrainedModel._init_weights` initializes the parameters of **child** modules by name —
`module.q_proj.weight`, `module.fc1.weight`, `module.text_projection.weight`, and so on. A quantized
checkpoint replaces `weight` on those children with packed tensors (`weight_packed` for
compressed-tensors, `qweight` for GPTQ/AWQ), so loading one raises

```
AttributeError: 'Linear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

from the initialization pass that runs at the end of loading: `_finalize_model_loading` →
`_initialize_missing_keys` → `initialize_weights` → `smart_apply` → `_init_weights`
(`modeling_utils.py:4517`, `:2476-2491`). For a packed format the packed layout is installed **before**
the weights are loaded, by `transformers` itself —
`CompressedTensorsHfQuantizer._process_model_before_weight_loading` calls
`self.compressor.compress_model(model)` (`quantizers/quantizer_compressed_tensors.py:117-121`).

A container such as `CLIPAttention` owns no parameter of its own, so `_initialize_weights`' skip
conditions never apply to it for a class living in `transformers.*`, and it always reaches
`_init_weights`.

This PR routes every child-weight initialization in `CLIPPreTrainedModel._init_weights` through a
small helper that skips a child with no `weight`, which is the guard the generic
`PreTrainedModel._init_weights` already applies to `nn.Linear`/`nn.Conv*` (`modeling_utils.py:2392`)
and to the norms (`:2418-2421`, *"Norms can exist without weights"*). It is the same shape as the
merged #38013, which fixed this class of failure in `modeling_qwen2_5_omni.py` for AutoAWQ
checkpoints.

`MetaClip2PreTrainedModel` inherits this method through modular and the converter inlines the body,
so `models/metaclip_2/modeling_metaclip_2.py` is regenerated in the same commit
(`python utils/modular_model_converter.py --files_to_parse src/transformers/models/metaclip_2/modular_metaclip_2.py`);
MetaCLIP-2 gets the fix with it.

Initialization of a non-quantized model is unchanged: the seeded `state_dict` of a tiny `CLIPModel`
hashes to the same SHA-256 before and after the patch (`a6808d27…`). The change also removes a
pre-existing crash for `CLIPForImageClassification` with `num_labels == 0`, where `classifier` is an
`nn.Identity`.

### Verification

```
# the new regression test
pytest tests/models/clip/test_modeling_clip.py -k init_weights_with_quantized
  -> 1 passed          (with the patch)
  -> 1 failed, AttributeError: 'Linear' object has no attribute 'weight'   (with the patch reverted)

# the test files utils/tests_fetcher.py selects for this diff
pytest tests/models/clip/test_modeling_clip.py tests/models/metaclip_2/test_modeling_metaclip_2.py \
       tests/models/sam3/test_modeling_sam3.py tests/models/sam3_video/test_modeling_sam3_video.py \
       tests/models/vision_text_dual_encoder/test_modeling_vision_text_dual_encoder.py
  -> 869 passed, 960 skipped, 6 xfailed, 8 failed in 6m18s

# repo checks
python utils/checkers.py ruff_check, ruff_format, init_isort, sort_auto_mappings, modeling_structure
  -> all OK (ruff over the whole tree)
python utils/checkers.py <all REPO_CONSISTENCY_CHECKERS>
  -> All 17 checks passed
```

The 8 failures are all `test_multi_gpu_data_parallel_forward` (4 in the CLIP file, 4 in the MetaCLIP-2
file). They are pre-existing on this machine: the same 8 fail on the parent commit, and nothing else in
those five files fails.

The `types` checker fails identically on the parent commit with the `ty` version I have installed, so
it is not affected by this diff.

### Scope

The same pattern — `_init_weights` dereferencing a child module's `.weight`/`.bias` — is present in 83
of 488 `modeling_*.py` files on `main`, and I measured the identical `AttributeError` for `T5`,
`Mamba2`, `LLaVA` (CLIP vision tower) and `Gemma3` (SigLIP vision tower). The issue linked above has
the full analysis, including why marking the quantized modules `_is_hf_initialized` (as the
bitsandbytes/torchao/quanto/mxfp4/sinq integrations do) does not fix it, and why the 4.x
"skip a fully loaded subtree" rule does not either. I kept this PR to CLIP; happy to extend the guard
to the other families in whatever batching you prefer.

Not applicable — I am not a first-time contributor (#44983, #46277). Per the *Agentic contributions*

title: _init_weights crashes on quantized checkpoints for models that initialize child modules by name
body:
### System Info

```
- `transformers` version: 5.16.0.dev0 (source, main @ dfb1af66d4) and 5.15.0 (wheel)
                          the relevant code is byte-identical in both
- Platform: Linux-6.5.0-35-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
- Python version: 3.11.12
- Huggingface_hub version: 1.6.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
- Accelerate version: 1.12.0
- compressed-tensors version: 0.15.0.1
- PyTorch version (GPU?): 2.10.0+cu128 (True, RTX 4090)
```

Also reproduced against `transformers` 4.51.3 to establish the v4 -> v5 behaviour change (see below).

### Who can help?

@CyrilVallez (model loading / weight initialization), @molbap (vision models)

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [X] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [X] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

`CLIPPreTrainedModel._init_weights` initializes the parameters of **child** modules by name
(`models/clip/modeling_clip.py:417-428` for the attention/MLP projections, `:429-452` for the
contrastive projections and the classifier):

```python
elif isinstance(module, CLIPAttention):
    init.normal_(module.q_proj.weight, std=in_proj_std)   # not `module`'s own parameter
```

A quantized checkpoint replaces `weight` on those children with packed tensors — `weight_packed`
for compressed-tensors, `qweight` for GPTQ/AWQ — so that read raises. The script below puts a model
into exactly that state and then runs the initialization pass that `from_pretrained` runs at the end
of loading, so it needs no quantization library:

```python
import torch
from torch import nn
from transformers import CLIPConfig, CLIPModel
from transformers.models.clip.modeling_clip import CLIPAttention, CLIPMLP

config = CLIPConfig(
    text_config={"hidden_size": 32, "intermediate_size": 37, "num_hidden_layers": 2,
                 "num_attention_heads": 4, "vocab_size": 99, "max_position_embeddings": 64},
    vision_config={"hidden_size": 32, "intermediate_size": 37, "num_hidden_layers": 2,
                   "num_attention_heads": 4, "image_size": 30, "patch_size": 2},
    projection_dim=16,
)
model = CLIPModel(config)

# What a packed checkpoint leaves on a quantized Linear: no `weight`, packed tensors instead.
for module in model.modules():
    if isinstance(module, (CLIPAttention, CLIPMLP)):
        for child in module.children():
            if isinstance(child, nn.Linear):
                out_features, in_features = child.weight.shape
                del child._parameters["weight"]
                child.register_parameter("weight_packed", nn.Parameter(
                    torch.zeros(out_features, in_features // 8, dtype=torch.int32), requires_grad=False))

# Everything the checkpoint provides is flagged as loaded, as the loader does.
for param in model.parameters():
    param._is_hf_initialized = True
for module in model.modules():
    if hasattr(module, "_is_hf_initialized"):
        del module._is_hf_initialized

model._initialize_missing_keys(is_quantized=True)
```

```
AttributeError: 'Linear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

The same script crashes with `T5ForConditionalGeneration`, `Mamba2ForCausalLM`,
`LlavaForConditionalGeneration` and `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration` (packing the vision tower) once
the module classes in the filter are swapped — 5 families measured, all on `main`.

The state is not artificial: for a packed format, `CompressedTensorsHfQuantizer._process_model_before_weight_loading`
calls `self.compressor.compress_model(model)` **before** the weights are loaded
(`quantizers/quantizer_compressed_tensors.py:117-121`), and `_finalize_model_loading` then runs
`_initialize_missing_keys` → `initialize_weights` → `_init_weights` over the whole tree
(`modeling_utils.py:4517`).

### Expected behavior

Loading a quantized checkpoint should not raise. Initialization only needs to seed the keys the
checkpoint does not provide, and every value in a fully quantized checkpoint comes from the file.

### Root cause

`_initialize_weights` skips a module only if (`modeling_utils.py:2438-2461`):

1. `module._is_hf_initialized` is set, or
2. `is_custom_code` **and** every **direct** (`recurse=False`) parameter/buffer is flagged.

A container such as `CLIPAttention` owns no parameter of its own, so under `is_custom_code=False` —
i.e. for every class living in `transformers.*` — it always reaches `_init_weights`, which then reads
its children's `weight`.

`transformers` 4.51.3 did not do this. `set_initialized_submodules` (`modeling_utils.py:584-598`)
marked a module `_is_hf_initialized` when its **recursive** `state_dict()` keys were all present in
the checkpoint, which is vacuously satisfied for a container whose children are all loaded. Measured,
same scenario as above:

| | 4.51.3 | 5.15.0 / main |
|---|---|---|
| CLIP, 24 packed Linears | parents 8/8 marked initialized → **no error** | **AttributeError** |
| T5, 32 packed Linears | parents 10/10 marked initialized → **no error** | **AttributeError** |

### Scope

An AST scan of `main` finds **83 of 488** `modeling_*.py` files whose `_init_weights` dereferences a
child module's `.weight`/`.bias`, including `siglip`, `siglip2`, `t5` (+ `mt5`, `umt5`, `longt5`,
`switch_transformers`, `udop`, `pix2struct`, `t5gemma`), `mamba`, `mamba2`, `falcon_mamba`,
`recurrent_gemma`, `kosmos2`, `phi4_multimodal`, `git`, `clvp`, `groupvit`, `owlvit`, `owlv2`,
`altclip`, `chinese_clip`, `clipseg`, `x_clip`, `align`, `detr`, `conditional_detr`, `maskformer`,
`oneformer`, and the MoE routers of `qwen3_next` / `qwen3_5_moe` / `qwen3_omni_moe`. Whether a given
family crashes depends only on whether the dereferenced child is among the quantized modules.

None of this duplication is linked by `# Copied from`, so `check_copies` neither propagates a fix nor
flags the divergence.

For a real-world profile: the public checkpoint `simaai/Gemma3-SigLIP448-GPTQ-Safetensors` is
compressed-tensors `pack-quantized` with an empty `ignore` list and `config_groups` that name
`model.vision_tower.encoder.layers.*.self_attn.{q,k,v,out}_proj` and `.mlp.{fc1,fc2}` explicitly —
the module set whose packing I measured to crash `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration`. I did not download
that checkpoint, so I am reporting the config match, not a load I ran.

### Two alternatives that do not work

Both were measured, in case they come up:

- **Marking the quantized modules `_is_hf_initialized`**, which `integrations/bitsandbytes.py`,
  `torchao.py`, `quanto.py`, `mxfp4.py` and `sinq.py` all do, does not help: the flag stops
  `_initialize_weights` from visiting that child, but the parent's `_init_weights` branch reaches into
  it by name anyway. Same `AttributeError` with and without the flag.
- **Restoring the v4 "skip a fully loaded subtree" rule** does not fix CLIP.
  `_move_missing_keys_from_meta_to_device` re-creates every non-persistent buffer with
  `torch.empty_like` (`modeling_utils.py:4768-4772`) and `_load_parameter_into_model` (`:518-525`)
  does not flag them, so a module with a non-persistent buffer anywhere in its subtree can never be
  skipped. CLIP has two (`position_ids` in `CLIPTextEmbeddings` / `CLIPVisionEmbeddings`), so
  simulating that rule on a fully loaded `CLIPModel` still runs `_init_weights` on the root, on both
  towers and on both embedding modules (5 modules out of 66 for a tiny config), which moves the
  `AttributeError` from `CLIPAttention` to the `CLIPModel` branch (`module.text_projection.weight` —
  a plain `nn.Linear`, and packed by any `Linear`-targeting scheme) rather than removing it. It does
  fully cover T5 (0/103 modules run) and Mamba2 (0/22), but a decoder-only model keeps rotary
  non-persistent buffers, so the root branch always runs there too (Llama: 3/33). A per-branch guard
  in the model file is the only thing that holds regardless.

### Proposed fix

The guard the generic `PreTrainedModel._init_weights` already applies to `nn.Linear`/`nn.Conv*`
(`modeling_utils.py:2392`) and to the norms (`:2418-2421`, "Norms can exist without weights"), applied
to the child dereferences as well. This is the shape of the merged #38013, which fixed the same class
of failure in `modeling_qwen2_5_omni.py` for AutoAWQ checkpoints.

PR #47921 does that for CLIP (and MetaCLIP-2, which inlines the method through modular). Two smaller
pieces are left for follow-ups, unless you would rather see them folded in:

- the `nn.Embedding` branch of the generic `_init_weights` (`modeling_utils.py:2402-2406`) is the one
  branch there that is still unguarded, so a checkpoint with quantized embeddings raises
  `AttributeError: 'Embedding' object has no attribute 'weight'` even with the CLIP fix applied;
- `modeling_clip.py:172`, `:208` and `:239` read `position_embedding.weight` / `patch_embedding.weight`
  in `forward`, so for a packed embedding or patch embedding the fix above moves the failure from load
  time to first forward rather than removing it.

Happy to extend the same guard to the rest of the 83 families in whatever batching you prefer.

### Disclosure

This report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). Every number, line reference and failure
above was produced by running the code against the installed packages. The reproduction script is
inlined above; the variants for the other families differ only in the model class and the module
filter. I am the author of the analysis and the patch, and I ran the verification myself.

title: Fix/bitsandbytes caching allocator warmup
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47919)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47919)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #47914 
caching_allocator_warmup crashes with AttributeError when loading a bitsandbytes-quantized model with a PEFT adapter (or any scenario where _load_pretrained_model runs after the model has been quantized).

Main changes:
* Renamed is_hqq_or_quark → is_quant_method_with_non_standard_params to reflect the broader purpose
* Added QuantizationMethod.BITS_AND_BYTES to the exemption set

Because:
bitsandbytes' Int8Params stores its internal quantization tensors (SCB, CB) as plain Python attributes, not via register_parameter() or register_buffer(). When expand_device_map produces entries like layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.base_layer.SCB, the warmup path calls get_parameter_or_buffer() on them and fails and crashes: AttributeError: 'layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.base_layer.SCB' is neither a parameter, buffer, nor extra state. caching_allocator_warmup already skips the warmup entirely for HQQ and Quark, precisely because those quantization methods also keep internal tensors outside the canonical PyTorch parameter/buffer registries. The BITS_AND_BYTES method is missing from that exemption list, so we need to add it up.
